Because at the end of the day we should come to the confusion point, Your Honours. Where we shall have a number of dispatches allegedly where author is Mr. Zupljanin, but it is not in fact the case, according to the page 26, line 10, and the testimony of this witness. Where we shall, of course, go in more details in our cross-examination, but, I mean, at this stage, I think it's -- it's quite sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pantelic, that it is a very common practice and, indeed, a necessary practice, that the chief of any institution would see letters and dispatches going out in his name and, of course, also thereby taking responsibility for the -- such letters and dispatches that are issued in his name, even if the chief of the institution didn't author the -- the documents itself. I think this is very normal administrative practice and, of course, the chief of the institution will have to rely on the skills and the faithfulness of his staff. Now, when these documents are being presented by the Prosecution and -- and we have the person who, in this case, authored some of the documents, the dispatches that we have seen and who signed them on behalf of your client, and when we admit these documents, the first thing that follows from our admission into evidence is, of course, that the document is authentic. It was, indeed, the document that was send. But the second thing that happens is that it goes into evidence also with its contents, and, I mean, this is a fact of life, that these documents were issued in the name of your client, and if it turns out that the there's something incriminating in these documents, then you will have to fight it. But you cannot refuse that they go into evidence. Am I getting myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, and in general terms, I am along your lines also. As I said, I don't have any particular problems that the number of dispatches will be admitted on a basis of MFI. I don't have problem. But, Your Honour, only dispatches where this witness is the author and signatory, then, I mean, also I don't have problem to be admitted with the full exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Where is the distinction you make? This witness, the author, and the other ones are what then? I mean, I just try to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will try to be clearer. For example, there are some dispatches where a signature is Mr. Zupljanin, but the author was chief of criminal department where, I don't know, certain informations were sent, et cetera, et cetera. I think the proper way to know with these codes that Mr. Hannis just mentioned, 01, 02, 03, 04, at certain stage, we could see who actually was the author of this particular dispatch and who put the name of Mr. Zupljanin. Again, Your Honour, I don't have in quality terms any problems with the professional aspect of work of my client, but as a matter of principle, I think it is not fair to admit dispatches where this particular witness is not aware of the -- who -- who made that particular dispatch. That's why we have certain codes, 01, 02, 03, et cetera, et cetera, depending of the departments of the CSB, and then we know who the author is, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The document -- the -- when the witness returns to the stand, the documents may be admitted as exhibits, as the Prosecution has -- has applied.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I understand correctly, what I propose -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry. This will be Exhibit P1003, Your Honours. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, your application was in respect of a particular document. The -- having regard to the discussion that that provoked, wouldn't it be practical to seek to admit the whole batch of documents and -- so that we can get on with the substance of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to do that, Your Honour. My list is in chronological order. The majority of the dispatches are sort of regular in form with what we have seen so far. I have a some particular questions about a few of them, but it would be nice if I could give you a list of 20 and say, These are all the same as the others, and I would tender them at that point in time, and then have them numbered and ask particular questions about them. I have a total, I think, of something less than 30. There are a few in there that are not dispatches from CSB Banja Luka but to Banja Luka, perhaps from the ministry, for example, for from an SJB, so I might have to treat those differently. But as far as the ones that are dispatches done by the teletypist we've seen and as described by the witness, I would like to put those in sort of as a lump collection, in light of the comments we've made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... for the record, no doubt, counsel for the Defence would wish to enter their objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a suggestion. From the material I have seen on the 65 ter list, these dispatches should be grouped by type, because there are dispatches sent from the Banja Luka centre, others who are received in some other centre, some received from the ministry or sent from the ministry, so that to admit them all together, I think is too ambitious. I realize the Court wishes to save time, but, in addition to this chronological order, I think they ought to be classified by type, because this would be of assistance, I believe, both for the Prosecutor and for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: For the record, we would enter our objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hannis, it appears to us that Mr. Krgovic's suggestion has some merit, so at some -- at your very earliest convenience, perhaps you can organise the documents in -- classify them in some fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I guess I will do that. I think it might be just as quick now for me to go through them one by one. And those are similar to the ones that we have been talking about, if I have some special question for the witness, I will ask him that question about that marking. But otherwise, I'm just going to move to tender it. If it's from CSB Banja Luka forwarded to the CSB -- CSB -- I'm sorry, the SJBs, I'll tender them. And others I'll treat differently. Ones from the -- from MUP headquarters or from a SJB to the centre, I'll treat differently and ask further questions before moving to tendered them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, we were thinking that perhaps if you would be good enough to organise the 30-odd dispatches in such a way as to classify them into groups, say, to the CSB and from the CSB, and -- and whatever useful classification or organisation we could make, then we would suggest that you simply have them moved into evidence now. You can still put one or two of some of them to the witness, if have you any particular point that you wish to raise with the witness. But, otherwise, for the sake of convenience and expediency, we will just admit them now, and then can you subsequently provide us with a list of the dispatches in the organised manner that you see fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm having a hard time figuring out mechanically how to best do that, now standing on my feet. If -- And part of I'm trying to do is, for example, in P1003 that we've just admitted, you will see in the first paragraph, it says: "We are hereby sending the integral text of order number 01-1/92. That document is the next one I intend to show because it links to this document, but it is not a CSB document. I think it makes most sense to connect it with a document which refers to it directly. I'm sorry, I appreciate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, no, let's just go ahead and move on now, but do it as quickly and swiftly as you possibly can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, before we leave this document, you will see in the first paragraph after the addressees, it says: "We are hereby sending you the integral text of order number 01-1/92, dated 4 May, which we received from the minister." Do you see that? I need to you answer out loud. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of May? The 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. But in the text. Under the addressees, it says, We're sending you the text, and then order number such and such, dated the 4th of May, which we received from the minister. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now can we show the witness exhibit 65 ter 106, dated the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on this one do you see that this is a document from the Ministry of the Interior numbered 01-1/92?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by the heading, you can see what it says here, Serbian republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Sarajevo. And there is a number, and there is a date. And what follows is the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: And what follows is the text. I don't know what there is at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the last page. See a name and a signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recognise the signature. It says, Minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic. I don't see anything to indicate it might have been signed by someone else. I don't recognise -- well, I'm not familiar, in other words, with Mr. Stanisic's signature. It appears to be -- well, I don't know who signed it, actually. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to tender this document as directly linked to P1003 that's now in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe we should take the opportunity to discuss this with Mr. Hannis during the break. We have no problem with the content of this document but, in principle, we have a general objection to the manner of its tendering, because the witness should identify this document: Is it a telegram, is it a dispatch, in other words?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the part that's missing, in addition to the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can I just ask one thing? Is the witness able to tell us that this was the attachment to the dispatch you are linking it with? In this way, that he can -- he can tell us that the dispatch -- that the dispatch and the attachment were processed in his centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for this particular document, it's the Prosecution position he doesn't need to. The documents themselves do that. You will see P1003 says, We're sending you the integral text of document number such and such, dated 4th of May. Then a quote from the text. You read the quoted text in P1003, and you see it is identical to the text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I don't think we understand each other. My question is not whether the witness remembers but whether this is -- this just -- this would be the normal procedure. I just want to know that this is -- it is more or less obvious, but I want so have the confirmation that this is what happens. If that is in a dispatch that hereby we send you, et cetera, et cetera, that the attachment goes through his services as well. For instance, would it be -- would it be encrypted? Would there be a necessity to have it encrypted? Would the attachment be encrypted as well? So my question is, does -- does this attachment -- did this attachment go through his centre or not? Or did he only make the dispatch and send the dispatch to, I don't know what other service, where -- where in the other service they attached it? It's just a question. I don't know -- I don't say it is crucial to the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand. Let me ask him a question, and then maybe you will see whether I'm understanding or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, if we can go back and look P1003, the one that we were just looking at. And basically this is a document being forwarded from the centre in Banja Luka, and it's forwarding a -- it's forwarding the text of an order that it says was received from the minister. Do you have the document in front of you yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I can hand the witness a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is still not on the screen, and the witness does not have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you see, Witness, the information that begins in the quotation mark. And my English translation says: "Given the reliable report [sic] that certain Ustasha forces, acting on Izetbegovic's instructions are attempting to recruit ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: From where would you, in the communications centre, have received that information to put in your outgoing dispatch? Would you have a document in hand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Look, you see the heading. It's our centre's dispatch. It's indicated to whom it should go. Then it says from the minister of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of BH, we received order number so-and-so, that we transmit to you in its entirety. That means that this part of the text had to be attached. Otherwise, it couldn't have been transmitted. Our service typed out one bit and then included this other part. We didn't have computers to copy and paste. I'm just typing out something that had arrived already. And then after the signature, where it says the minister, you just add, Please act on this, and so and so. Otherwise, it couldn't work. Nobody could have retyped this. You couldn't just glue this piece of paper on. I suppose it's a document. It -- it wasn't probably even a dispatch. It was some document. We received a document, and that document was typed out again ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now let me go back to 65 ter 106.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure when the time for the break is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] you have another six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Rakovic, I want to show that you document that appears to be from the minister of the interior. It has that same reference number and the date of May the 4th that we were looking at. This document itself, based on what I've seen and we've been talking about, that this does not appear to be a dispatch. This is not a teletype -- tele-printed document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I looked at it a moment ago. The second page of this document ends with a signature. Page 2 of this document, didn't we see it a moment ago on the screen? There was a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, we can put it on the screen for you. If we go to the last page. There did appear to be a signature.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: And you see that this document wasn't sent by the Security Services Centre. You can see where it come from. It had come from the ministry in Sarajevo as indicated at the top. And, secondly, it wasn't communicated through this system. You see the signature which means it could have been faxed, or it could have been copied and sent by mail. So it couldn't have been received through our system of encryption. As soon as you see the signature, you know that it is not our system. You can see the name and surname and signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you two questions about that. One, could this document that we see on the screen have been sent to the communications centre in the ministry and from which a teletype was prepared and sent to your centre? Is that one possibility how could you is gotten this information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Parallel to the signed version?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we heard testimony before when he explained how a document got sent by teletype. It was prepared by someone, perhaps the chief or his secretary, signed, delivered to the communications centre, then typed up into the teletype machine by the operator. And the original document then was initialed and returned to the author. I think I'm stating that correctly. So I'm asking if, in the MUP headquarters, in the ministry, this could be the document that was authored by, apparently, Mico Stanisic, delivered to their communication centre from which a dispatch was prepared. The other possibility that I intend to ask him about is whether or not this actual document itself was mailed or delivered by courier to Banja Luka. But somehow they had the information that is contained in this document obviously. I'm just trying to explore the possible means of how it got there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess the issue is rather whether this witness was taking part in the processing of the document, in the communications processing, whether it went through his office somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me it must have, because the contents of are contained within an outgoing dispatch sent by his centre. So they must have gotten it from somewhere. Am I missing something?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honours haven't had a chance to read the text in Mico Stanisic's document to compare with what goes in the outgoing fax. The outgoing fax contains the identical information that's in Mico Stanisic's document. Therefore, in Banja Luka, they must have had a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We are still talking about 65 ter 106; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the document is admitted and marked. And it is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1004, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As the witness is coming in, Your Honours, I would indicate that I have gone through my list. I have identified 14 documents that I see as being outgoing dispatches from CSB Banja Luka. My Case Manager has created a list. We'll send to the legal officer and to the Defence, and perhaps they can have a look and advise whether they have an objection to those. The other documents are either from a CSB or incoming -- incoming to the CSB from an SJB or from the ministry, or otherwise not like these, and I need to treat those separately, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So I will skip dealing with outgoing CSB documents for now and concentrate on the others until I hear from the Defence and the Your Honours about the remaining ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, if we could show the witness exhibit -- it's an exhibit in evidence, but I have a question for him. It's P565.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Rakovic, this document coming up on your screen is dated the 18th of May, 1992, and appears to be from a man named Zoran Josic, and it's directed to the CSB Banja Luka. Can you make any comment on this document? Is this what an incoming document from one of the SJBs would look like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, Banja Luka had its own public security station on an equal footing with others, but the largest one. And this Zoran Josic was, I suppose, I can't say that he was chief. He says head of section, Zoran Milosevic. He was head of the section at the public security station in the criminal department, I suppose. And he is sending a dispatch to the CSB Banja Luka, the SNB sector which is national security sector. I don't know what this would mean. SB -- since CSB Banja Luka was divided into two sectors, public security and national security. It used to be state security. But at that time it was national security. It says, your reference, dispatch such and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, let me ask you a question. In the CSB in Banja Luka, did communication documents to and from the national security side go through your communications centre, or did they have a separate communications centre; do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: When I started working, documents sent by the state security, or to the state security, if they went through this system -- they mainly went through our system, the teletype system. I cannot associate anything with this dispatch because both seats were there so it probably didn't go through us. It was printed, signed, and then the secretaries probably took it from one room to another; that's the way I see it. But, otherwise, generally speaking, most dispatches during my tenure were processed by us even for the State Security Service, although by that time, they were already separating and creating their own computer system. But for the most part, dispatches for them and by them were processed by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Banja Luka SJB, where was that located vis-a-vis Banja Luka CSB? Were you in the same building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: The public security Banja Luka, the crime police and the chief were in the same building. In addition to the crime police and the chief, there were also police stations in Banja Luka. At that time we had three police stations, and the traffic police station, PC centre, PC Bucak, and another one, and that was all SJB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Two more questions on this document. At the top, number 11-2/02, what does that tell you about what unit or person it comes from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Eleven is the centre; -2 could mean SJB Banja Luka; /02 is crime police; 01 was uniform police; and 02 was crime police. And the rest is clear. You can see that the head of section sent it to the addressee indicated above.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for clarity, the English says: Reference your dispatch number 11-1401. I think from the original you can see that should be 11-140. I don't know if we need to send it for a corrected translation, or if we can just note it on the record that the English should be 140. And I would indicate 11-140 is a document in evidence as P561. Next if we could show the witness 65 ter 442.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Rakovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This appears to be a document from the Prijedor SJB addressed to the Banja Luka Security Services Centre to the head and to the operative duty service. First of all, can you tell us what the operative duty service is in Banja Luka CSB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the operative duty service at the CSB Banja Luka was a duty service that worked 24 hours/7 doing mostly police work, and it also coordinated with other public security stations, as far as I know. At that time, and they are doing that still today, they gathered information, they prepared morning bulletins, and they continue to do the same today. We see the person who sent this was from CSB Prijedor, and a person from CSB Prijedor has signed. But normally you should write "chief" first among the addressees and then operative duty service. At that time and today the operative duty service would work round the clock, and there would be two duty officers, and they practically stand in for the management and coordinate. Still today when a dispatch arrives from the -- from whoever for the chief or chief of sector, we give these dispatches to the operative duty service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm running short on my time, and I need to stop you there. We need to focus on 1992. At the bottom of this page I see something that is translated as 2 June 1992, Dusko, CSB, at 20/20 hours; and then Dragan, operative duty service, at 2025 hours. Do you know who those individuals are and what that notation refers to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: From what I see, I suppose this first item means that at 20/20, Dusko, the signalsman received the dispatch, and at 2025, he gave it to Dragan, the operative officer on duty, because I don't know any other Dusko. We have the date, the time, and Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this apparently is not a document sent by teletype because we see handwritten number and signature. So how would this document have come in to the CSB? Via courier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Looking at this document, I don't see any indication that it came by fax. Because with faxes you always get to see the number from which it was sent. It must have come -- it's possible that it came in some other way and that other way -- if it is obviously not from dispatch traffic and there is a signature and it's not a fax, it could have come by courier. I'm not sure, but I can't think of any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender 442.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The witness is still sure -- is nevertheless sure that this is a document that was processed in his centre. He recognised it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think he indicated the signature saying received for persons who worked in the CSB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. I missed that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness was not asked the basic question, whether there is evidence it had been received by the centre, to make the connection between the witness and the document because this is not a telegram. This is just the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, my argument --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The witness seems -- wished to add something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to come back to this paper, the Honourable Judge asks if it was done in our centre. Obviously it was not processed at our centre. We certainly did not receive it through our means of communication. I thought, since Dusko was signed that it may have arrived by mail or some other way to our centre. Maybe directly to the operative duty service. I don't know who this Dusko could be. I know one Dusko who worked in communications. Because we had the operations duty service and the communication service that worked 24 hours a day. So if somebody came in the evening or at night, they would have no one to hand the document to. It could have arrived -- it could have been handed in to communications, then Dusko would sign for it, and five minutes later he would hand it to the operations duty service. That's how I thought our communication section could have been involved. But we can't see anything else. We see it didn't go through dispatch traffic. It doesn't mean that it had arrived at all. It could have been copied anywhere. There is no signature of the recipient. We see just Dragan, operations duty officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rakovic. Mr. Hannis, the answer that the witness volunteered, doesn't this give substance to Mr. Krgovic's objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it does give some substance. Maybe I can ask the witness one further question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you telling us now, sir, that you seriously doubt that this document was received in CSB Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by this, you can't make a conclusion because there's no signature. There's no signature. It says Dusko and Dragan. Some Dusko and some Dragan. If somebody had signed, then we could say, Yes, it was received at the operations duty service. I'm just talking about assumptions that somebody could have handed this to this Dusko who worked in my section, and then Dusko could have given it to Dragan in the operations duty service. And it's addressed to the operations duty service. I'm not talking that it was received. I'm just saying that this is what could have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, doesn't it leave you sort of stranded in terms of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Pending?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Pending some further verification by another individual in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose so. Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1005, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show the witness now exhibit 9 -- I'm sorry, Exhibit P654. It's dated the 25th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, what can you tell us about this document? Is this a dispatch that went out from your centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: From what I see, that's what it looks like. There is an heading, an indication to whom it was addressed, there is a reference to an earlier dispatch number, 11-140, and we see the chief of the centre at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: It went by teletype, DX. We see it was an open dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can we now have a look at 65 ter 412?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The one that we were just showing you was asking about asking the CSBs to carry out their obligations about the delivering plans for confiscation of illegally-owned weapons. And now 65 412 is a document dated 25th of May. Same day as the previous document. Do you see this? Is this a dispatch or the original document that would have been sent to be dispatched? What can you tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what it would look like, a document from which a dispatch has to be created. It should be sent in the form of dispatch through our system. It's obviously that SJB Prijedor sent it, but the signatory is not exactly the chief of the SJB. Somebody signed for him. If it had been sent through our dispatch communications, then there would have been no signature. If it had been a fax, there would have been a header indicating the fax. So I suppose this was something that was just prepared for sending but never went anywhere. Well, maybe it was sent. Maybe the dispatch went out, but we don't see the part that was transmitted. But this is obviously a draft. Another typical thing, another noteworthy thing, you see there's a mark at the top, PS Roman numeral II-10. I think somebody scrolled on this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You have no idea what that marking would mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, it could be PS police station. What the Roman numeral II means, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the number on this document, 11-12. Do you know -- 11-12 refers to Prijedor SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Eleven is the centre, and 12 is the SJB Prijedor, like number 2 was SJB Banja Luka. These numbers indicated the public security station in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me next --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may have I that marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The previous document, had that been previously -- was that exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It had, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1006, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned fax machines. I'd like to show you 65 ter number 144. This is dated the 29th of May. This appears to an outgoing document from CSB Banja Luka. And can you tell us how this was transmitted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the copy of this document, I see the initial mark is that of our centre. I see in the header it's addressed to the chief, but I also see that somebody signed for the chief of the centre using the number indicating the chief's office. I'm not reading the document. If I read it, I would probably find out it was created by the crime police. I think it was the crime police who wrote this, because they mentioned robberies, breaking and entering, et cetera. And somebody sent this out on behalf or under the name of the chief, and it was sent by fax, because it shows our fax number, 7839155; that was our fax number. I can't see anything else. It didn't go by dispatch. I see DX, which means it was a normal dispatch. CSB, to everyone in the region. Whether everyone was able to receive it is another matter. I don't think everyone had fax machines. Maybe some stations typed this out and sent it to other stations which did not have a fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question about that. Where was the fax machine located? Was that in your comm. centre, in your area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in our centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: It was where the teleprinters were. I didn't see it often.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. If -- if there was a SJB that did not have a fax machine by which to receive a fax document like this, wouldn't there be some indication on this document that alternate means of transmission were made for that SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, the sender never did this unless they were sending a document. They would mostly send a message to us, and if on the document it said it had to be encrypted, then we certainly wouldn't have sent it by fax. But as the document is open, there's no marking so that means it was open, we were able to send it by other means of communication, including a fax. So it's possible that somebody received it by fax or by some other means.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But my question is, in your comm. Centre, the operator or the comms. worker who got this document and sent it out by fax, if there was not a fax machine in a particular SJB so that it could be received by fax, wouldn't there have been some notation or indication that alternate means were used to send this document to that SJB by courier or by some other means? Didn't you have to keep a record of what you sent out so that you could prove to the author that the requested document had been sent to all the addressees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: If it was not possible to send the document to all the addressees, then when the original dispatch was being sent back, the operator would inform the sender that the dispatch could not be sent to one or more of the addressees. He would know to whom he had not been able to send it and he would make a note of that. The sender, in that case, might think that, Well, it wasn't absolutely necessary to send it to that particular addressee, or he might decide to use some other means of communication, or mail it, or send it by courier, or if he had a teleprinter available, he could have it re-typed and sent by teleprinter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender 144.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1007, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we next show the witness 65 ter 2571.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Rakovic, this is a document dated the 22nd of June, 1992. And it appears that you were the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Two questions. At the bottom, the last line is translated as, Received by, question mark, Sunkic, on 22 June at certain hours. Do you know who he was and where he worked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Vidosav Sunkic, I think his first name was Vidosav, was a retired employee of our service. He had worked there before I came. He was probably engaged as a reservist because he was a reserve police officer. He had previously worked on communications in RT Tej.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Then we see some handwritten information on the top in the upper right. I see there's a number 11-12/513. I think you agreed with me before that 11-12 appears to be the number associated with SJB Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the numbers up here and the names I see written here, I think it was the SJB Prijedor, yes. I sent it to the chief of the Banja Luka CSB for his information, to the chiefs of the SJBs on the ground, all of them, and to the communications departments of the SJBs. The larger ones had their comms. departments, Prijedor and so on, and the text you see here is one that I wrote and sent out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The names in handwriting at the top, Jankovic, D; Mijic, R; and Jankovic, M, are names you associate with Prijedor SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, there was a Jankovic and a Mihic working in Prijedor, and they probably added these names to their dispatches, and they might have copied the dispatch and given it to other people so they would learn how to send dispatches, because that was the point of this whole dispatch that I sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender 2571.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1008, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if next we could show the witness 65 ter 488.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this is a document dated the 24th of July, 1992, purportedly from Prijedor to the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. Can you tell us anything about the handwriting at the bottom on the left? There's a date and the name "Rodic." Do you know who that might be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I can assume that it was the only Rodic who was in comms., and he is still employed there. He probably received it at 1950 hours and signed it. You can see that it arrived from Prijedor. It was addressed to the Banja Luka CJB, and a man called Djuro Prpos was authorised, probably he worked there. But the only thing that is not clear is how this dispatch arrived there. So signature there. I don't -- well, it couldn't have come through the system bearing this signature because you can say by authorisation and everything else, but then you can't initial it, so it didn't come through or teleprinter system. I don't see any fax numbers here either of any sender or addressees, so in view of the time entered here, I am assuming it might have been sent by courier. Somebody might have brought it along who was coming to visit our centre on other business, perhaps, and Rodic received it and then forwarded it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the circle are two letters that are in my English translation as BM. Do you know what that would stand for in this context, under Rodic's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I see that, but I don't know what it means. I know that Rodic's first name is Milorad. So what BM might be, I don't know. I couldn't tell you. Everything else is familiar. I see the time, the date, the name. I assume it's our Rodic, not another Rodic. This was done in the afternoon or in the evening. I know that five or six years ago there was a Rodic in operative -- doing operative duty service, and he retired. Whether it might that be Rodic, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether or not this document was received in your security centre in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said just now, I cannot confirm that. If this Rodic is my Rodic, the one who worked under me, then, yes. But it doesn't say here what Rodic it was, and it didn't come through the teleprinter system. So I can't see any evidence that it came through our system. I don't see our fax number here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: There might have been somebody else whose last name was Rodic, although there was a Rodic working under me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you next 65 ter 1264.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Is this being marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P1009, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could have 65 ter 1264.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can tell you, Mr. Rakovic, this is a document dated the 3rd of August, 1992. This appears to an outgoing document from your centre and the -- the written name of the author is Sreto Gajic. Did you know Sreto Gajic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Sreto Gajic, yes. But I can't see that this could have been sent from the CSB. I see the number, yes, 11-1/01. Whether he was using the number of the uniformed police department, I don't know. But this doesn't seem to make sense. The MUP of the Serbian republic of Bosnia Herzegovina to the minister Sarajevo and then CSB. Well, this seems to have been written unprofessionally. CSB Banja Luka is on the right-hand side, maybe it should have been on the left-hand side, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Then would you have to state the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Stop. I just asked if you knew Sreto Gajic. Please just answer my question, and let me move on to the next question. Mr. Gajic was an inspector from the ministry that came out to Banja Luka to conduct an inspection in connection with the special unit. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. I knew Sreto Gajic superficially. I thought he was working in the border police, but I wasn't sure. All I'm sure of that is that he was a member of the police force, but whether he was working in the centre, or the ministry, I really don't know. I know we met, said hello, but I'm not sure exactly where he worked. He was not in a position of leadership or authority, so I didn't really -- I don't recall. It says here chief of the department for organisation and mobilisation. I had no idea there was such a department in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure there was. Do you know if there was such a department in the ministry, at the higher level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know about that even less. To the best of my knowledge, there was no such department where we were. But I know even less about what there was at the ministry. I was very far away from the ministry, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If Mr. Gajic is an inspector carrying out work on behalf of the ministry in your centre and he wanted to send a dispatch or telegram back to the ministry, how would he go about it? Wouldn't he have to work through you your people, your comms. centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: If it arrived through the system, then he would have had to send it through us. It looks like it might have been a dispatch. Maybe he used the number of the uniformed police, and somebody might have brought it along with his signature on it, up to the centre, and it's possible that someone sent it, but I really couldn't know that. But nobody could come from the outside and send a dispatch from our office. Only our staff members were authorised to send dispatches. Nobody could just walk in and send a personal message, for example. It all had to be entered into the log-book, it all had to be registered, signed --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This has a number on top of 11-1/01. What unit or section would that be in your centre? Is that the uniformed police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying. It is all incomplete. It is 11-1, all right, that's the centre. Eleven is the centre. One, I know what it stands for. But 01 should stand fort uniformed police. And can you see he put CSB Banja Luka here and to whom it should be sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The individual named in the document, Tomo Mirosavic. Do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I've never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I have this marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked. Mr. Hannis, its -- we would be adjourning for the day in 30 minutes. Three minutes ago you had 40 minutes left, so by my arithmetic, that would give you about five minutes in the morning when we resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours you're aware of the difficulties I've had. I will -- I will try to my best to finish within that time. But part of it depends on the response I get from the Defence about the 14 or so documents that I am requesting to admit, sort of, en masse; meanwhile, I'll move through the remaining ones I have that are not in that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, one more question to the witness on this document, on the top of the right-hand side, there is DX and 0. Is that -- I didn't pay attention to it in other documents, but there are two different --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He can explain that, Your Honour. We did talk about DX as being one of the designations for level of urgency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yeah, and 0 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it talked about 0 -- also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a lower level. So can there be two levels at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He can answer that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: DX0 means DX open. Usually people omitted to say open. They would say DX, X with a diacritic, if it had to be encrypted, and they would usually not bother to put the 0 for open. So I'm saying whoever wrote this got mixed up, and this is all sloppily written.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1264 becomes P1010, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next one, could we show the witness 65 ter 521.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, this is a document that is headed Prijedor public security station. At the bottom, we see a signature for Chief Drljaca in the SJB, and on the left-hand side we see typed, chief of centre, Stojan Zupljanin. Can you tell us how this document came to be? Is this something that was sent and then Mr. Drljaca's name was added to it before it was put in the files or circulated to his subordinate units? Can you help us with that at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try. It is evident from this that the original dispatch was sent from the Prijedor public security, and that the author of the dispatch was someone who signed on behalf of Sime Drljaca. I don't know who that person might be. On the left where it says, chief of centre, Stojan Zupljanin, this is just typed here, and I don't see why or how. There's no system here. This is all topsy-turvy. It is all something that was not sent either by teleprinter, the ones we had, or by fax. I fail to understand this document. It says chief of centre on the left-hand side, and whereas it is being sent by the station. And the signature of the chief of the station, it's actually signed for him by someone else. But his name is there. And all of this really is something that I cannot explain at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm making no requests concerning that one then. I would like to show the witness 65 ter 1263. And perhaps -- this is a lengthy document. If the usher can hand him a hard copy, I may be able to move more quickly through it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Rakovic, this is a document that appears to be sent from the Ministry of the Interior to all the CSBs, SJBs, administrations at headquarters, and the national security. And it appears to be a request for information from all those units and individuals for the purposes of preparing an annual report, or at least for the past nine months. Did -- were you aware of this document in late 1992? Did you have to do any work as far as providing information for the preparation of an annual report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: It's evident that this document has a signature, it has a stamp. This is not the minister's signature, if the one we saw just before was. And they're asking for a report on work in 1992, and it says here exactly what the report should contain. I never saw this before my interviews here and proofing sessions, but I know that in my service, a brief version, a shorter version of such a dispatch might have arrived, because I know that, together with my fellow workers, we prepared such information. And if we view the ministry as the centre, I would have the stations send me reports on work for 1992. That was the usual practice, and it's still done today. There would be -- I didn't ask for information on crimes, but staffing documents, that was our line of work. That was what we asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can I have that marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry. That would be P1011, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could show the witness next exhibit in evidence, P395. This is a document dated the 12th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a document that is addressed to your group in the centre in Banja Luka. And it makes reference to a dispatch number, 11-1/04-01. Can you tell us who or what 11-1/04 in the centre was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: 11-1/04 is the section for communications and encryption that I led. At the top, SJB Sanski Most, on the request in this dispatch that I sent --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you, and try to keep it to short questions and short answers because I have limited time. So that was you. And this document appears to be a response to your dispatch that had been sent out the day before on the 11th of January seeking, it appears, information about the cryptographic data protection staff and devices and a survey of telegram flow. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, see what it says here: Overview of the status, overview of the documents, overview of the traffic of documents, everything fits. I asked the station to make this available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And on the last page, we see a summary of the number of dispatches sent and received, both open dispatches and encrypted dispatches, for the period from January 1, 1992, through December 31st, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. That's what was requested, and that's what they sent to the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about your regular reports about the work of your section. Do you recall preparing reports at the end of June or the beginning of July 1992 on the work of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember clearly whether I prepared them towards the end of June, but it's the usual practice to prepare monthly, six monthly and annual reports. The basic one was the monthly report. We, as the section, received reports from police stations on the amount of dispatches received and sent. That's the usual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show the witness Exhibit P595 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure this appears on my list, but it was indicated in an e-mail that was sent to Chambers and to Defence counsel as one of two additional documents I intended to use with this witness. Can I cite you to the e-mail and time and reference, if you need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's already exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is. Both of them are. I think by an e-mail dated 24th at 8.57 a.m., I indicated that I was going to use this one, P595, and also P261.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report on the work of your centre from 1 January until 30 June. And I would like to turn to page 11 of the English. And I believe in e-court, it's page 18 of the B/C/S. Yes, if we could scroll in the B/C/S page. Yes, thank you. Section 5.1 is the functioning of the communications system and cryptographic protection. Do you remember looking at this during proofing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I do. In proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. In does talk about some of the problems that were encountered and about, about six or seven lines down in my English, you will see the parentheses with the names of certain CSBs, Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Bosanska Krupa, et cetera. That sentence reads: "Due to war operations there were constant interruptions in telephone and telegraph links with some SJBs, and then it names those, and numerous breakdowns which were required as the situation would allow." Now I take it that since Sanski Most, Kotor Varos, Prijedor, and others are not named in this list, they didn't have that same kind of problem with numerous interruptions in telephone and telegraph links. Would that be a fair conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: If you read this more carefully, you can see that I, because I wrote this part of the report, say in the first part that there had been problems in teletype traffic. There were problems, interruptions, et cetera. And then I go on to say that interventions were made to repair breakdowns and to re-establish communications where there were not any. So there were none. There were no problems in Vakuf Kupres, et cetera. But in this existing system which worked, more or less, there were some problems. Whereas in the other areas, there was no communication system in Krupe, in Kupres, there were no communications. I went three times with telecom, I remember, to try to set up some sort of line towards -- through civilian authorities, so you could make one phone call a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Maybe there is a problem in translation. My English translation reads --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the witness is not accurate, so please ask the witness to repeat the answer, so that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your answer seemed to be saying that these named municipalities, Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Krupe, Glamoc, et cetera, were ones were there were not problems. As I read the document, those were the very SJBs where you had constant interruptions in telephone and telegraph links. Is that correct? Those were the ones where you had lots and lots of problems. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me read to you what is written exactly in Serbian. The activities in the area of communications and cryptographic protection was carried out --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... could you start at the sentence that says: "Due to war operations ..." That's the one I'm confused about. Could you start with that sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: It is below what I have been reading; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: yes. I think it's the third sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Which line is it? Which line from the status of communications is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, do you see the parentheses with the names of SJB Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Vakuf, Krupa, Kupres. Oh, I see. Due to war operations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to, but it is moving constantly. "Due to war operations" -- Now I have lost it again. Can you stop moving the text. Let me read. Due to war -- again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We're sorry, sir. The system is not functioning well. You will get a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Rakovic. I think it's in the area marked with the blue highlighter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll read slowly: "Due to war operations, there also occurred constant interruptions in TT communications with some public security stations (SJB Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Bosanska Krupa, Glamoc, Bihac, Teslic, Bosansko Grahovo, Drvar, Sipovo, Mrkonjic Grad, and others) as well as numerous break downs that were addressed to the best of our ability. In addition this problem there were shortages of electricity, fuel for power generators."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go do page 12 in the English, and, sir, at the bottom of the page that you were reading from. There's a number; it says how many total open telegrams were sent and received and how many coded telegrams were received and transmitted. Do you see those numbers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: I see, I see. In addition, 9.956 open dispatches were received; 9.686 were transmitted; 728 closed dispatches were received; 898 closed dispatches were transmitted; and 2.297 were in transit. That's what I wrote, and I suppose it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain to us what you mean about 2.297 were in transit. What is that? How is that different from received or sent? Are these ones that you simply forwarded on without any additional information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO RAKOVIC
utterances.text: In proofing, we discussed about this transit, and I wasn't quite clear myself what this category "transit" is supposed to cover. I can't really explain. I can't explain the term "transited." What could it be? Could it be extended communication or what? The chief probably gave me a ready formulation, and I just noted it down. I -- I really can't think of what it could be mean. Maybe we just sort of forwarded something that couldn't be sent directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know it is about five minutes early, but this has been a difficult session. I wonder if we could stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Rakovic, we're about do take the adjournment for today. Your testimony will continue tomorrow morning. We will resume at 9.00. Having been sworn as a witness, you cannot communicate with the lawyers from other side, and in such conversations as you may with persons outside of the Tribunal, you cannot discuss your testimony. Do you understand? Do you understand what I just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will take the adjournment now and resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of February, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.55 p.m.,
